newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Funds' weight in Tel Aviv stock market drops.
newsitem.headline: Funds' weight in Tel Aviv stock market drops.

text.p: Provident and mutual funds held 14.3 percent of shares traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) at the end of 1996 compared with 17.9 percent a year earlier, Meitav Investments and Securities said on Monday.

A study by the brokerage house showed both types of funds have been steadily hit by redemptions since 1994. Investors pulled 18.6 billion shekels out of mutual funds and 17.4 billion shekels from provident funds in the last three years.
Analysts have attributed the exodus to a sluggish stock market and relatively high interest rates offered by banks for shekel deposits.
"As a result, the weight of the funds in the stock market has dropped sharply," the report said.

At the end of 1996, provident funds held 9.5 percent of total market capitalisation compared with 11 percent a year earlier and mutual fund holdings in TASE fell to 4.8 percent from 6.9 percent, the study showed.
Meitav said the vacuum left by the funds was filled by investments made by foreigners and major shareholders in companies who increased their holdings.

The Bank of Israel said last month that total market capitalisation, not counting shares held by the Israeli government, rose slightly in 1996 to 98.02 billion shekels from 96.06 billion shekels a year earlier.
At the end of 1996 provident funds -- long-term savings funds with special tax benefits -- controlled assets worth 111 billion shekels while mutual funds held 14 billion shekels in assets.
